1q9x8jw:205: In traditional programming, the person writing code is also the intent holder, and tacit knowledge is automatically completed during implementation. In the AI era, the intent holder is still human, but the code writer has become the model—the model does not hold tacit knowledge and forgets when the session ends. The essence of a Spec is the minimal, verifiable explicit encoding of the "acceptable implementation space." Four keywords: minimal (constraints too thick makes maintenance cost approach that of code), explicit (rules not written down can only be guessed by AI), verifiable (what cannot be judged as right or wrong is not a Spec but a wish), implementation space (a Spec does not rewrite code but defines boundaries).

1u1ji98:241: Writing a Spec for AI is useless; writing it for the reviewer is useful. In the AI era, the implementer has been replaced by a model, but the reviewer is still human. SSD rule: The Spec's form primarily follows human review habits, while also ensuring AI can continue to consume it. The template has four parts: Background & Goals / System Design (sequence diagram + architecture diagram + solution selection) / Quality Assurance (AC table + risk review) / Release & Go-live.
